2610.08574.title: FedDermaSeg: Federated Learning for Dermatological Image Segmentation
2610.08574.paper_summary: Skin cancer is a major global health concern, and early detection and accurate lesion delineation are important for effective diagnosis and treatment planning. Automated skin lesion analysis can assist dermatologists, with lesion segmentation serving as a fundamental step in computer-aided diagnostic systems. Conventional deep learning-based segmentation models typically rely on centralized training, where images and their corresponding segmentation masks are collected on a central server. Such data aggregation raises privacy concerns in medical applications and requires substantial centralized computational resources. To address these limitations, we investigate the feasibility of federated learning for privacy-preserving skin lesion segmentation. The training and validation sets of the ISIC 2018 Skin Lesion Segmentation Challenge dataset are used to simulate a distributed learning environment and develop a federated segmentation model. The resulting model is evaluated on the ISIC 2018 test set and the PH2 dataset to assess its performance and generalizability. Experimental results demonstrate that the federated model achieves performance comparable to centralized training while consistently improving upon the locally trained models. These findings demonstrate the potential of federated learning for collaborative skin lesion segmentation without requiring centralized aggregation of medical images.
2610.08574.paper_summary_zh: 皮膚癌是全球健康的一個重大問題，早期檢測和準確的病變輪廓描繪對於有效的診斷和治療計劃至關重要。自動化的皮膚病變分析可以協助皮膚科醫生，病變分割作為計算機輔助診斷系統中的基本步驟。傳統的基於深度學習的分割模型通常依賴於集中式訓練，圖像及其相應的分割掩模會被收集到中央伺服器上。這種數據聚合在醫療應用中引發了隱私問題，並需要大量的集中計算資源。為了解決這些限制，我們探討了聯邦學習在隱私保護的皮膚病變分割中的可行性。使用ISIC 2018皮膚病變分割挑戰數據集的訓練和驗證集來模擬分佈式學習環境並開發聯邦分割模型。所得到的模型在ISIC 2018測試集和PH2數據集上進行評估，以評估其性能和泛化能力。實驗結果表明，聯邦模型的性能與集中式訓練相當，同時在本地訓練模型的基礎上持續改進。這些發現展示了聯邦學習在無需集中聚合醫療影像的情況下，進行協作皮膚病變分割的潛力。
